candidates.title: Recover access to existing workflows

demandEvidence.chore: Recover access to the original owner account and make existing workflows visible without losing them.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: How do I recover access to the original owner account / make my existing workflows visible again without losing them?

ease.reason: A student could format an operator-supplied recovery checklist, but this source gives no safe recovery procedure or implementation support.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: automation consultants might charge for recovery guidance; this request establishes neither a buyer nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock checklist is possible, but account ownership, platform support and preserving workflows require authorized human action.

autonomy.reason: The only safe bounded output is guidance for a person; account recovery and data preservation cannot run unattended on this evidence.

evidence.reason: The request explicitly states account access and workflow visibility recovery, but gives no procedure, frequency or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Assessed a checklist-only experiment; reject because the task depends on authorized platform recovery and protecting existing workflows, with no safe automation method in the evidence.

candidates.title: Draft replies to frequent customer queries

demandEvidence.chore: Handle frequent customer queries arriving through WhatsApp and email.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: We get 50–100 customer queries a day on WhatsApp and email, and want an AI agent to handle most of them.

ease.reason: A beginner could classify fictional queries and draft replies, but no supplied building reference supports channel setup.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a team handling many customer questions might pay for draft assistance; the request proves no purchase.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can use fictional queries for one category; production integrations, language quality and accuracy remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed loop can classify and draft repeatedly, while a person must check facts and approve every reply.

evidence.reason: The post states daily query volume across two channels and asks for an agent, but supplies no implementation reference.

candidates.reason: Reject as a duplicate of recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6 on the support inbox workflow dimension; its five provisional ratings also average below 6.

candidates.title: Prepare due date reminder drafts from a sheet

demandEvidence.chore: Use due dates in a spreadsheet to trigger reminders.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to connect Google Sheets to my Make scenario using the Search Rows module so I can automate reminders based on due dates stored in a spreadsheet.

ease.reason: A student can test operator-supplied sample rows and draft reminders, but no supplied building reference supports the connection.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional service operators might pay to reduce missed due dates; this request establishes no payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can turn synthetic due-date rows into drafts; live access and delivery remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed scheduled check could flag due rows, but a person must verify dates, recipients and messages.

evidence.reason: The request names spreadsheet due dates and reminders, but gives no implementation support or corroborated demand.

candidates.reason: Assessed a synthetic-row reminder experiment; its provisional mean is 4.6, below 6, and the snapshot adds no implementation evidence to prior assessments.
